result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.communicability()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Compute communicability between all pairs of nodes. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L14428-L14518){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.communicability(return_dict=True) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Communicability measures the "amount of communication" between pairs of nodes based on all walks between them, with shorter walks weighted more heavily. It uses the matrix exponential of the adjacency matrix: `exp(A)`. For nodes `u` and `v`, the communicability is: `C(u, v) = \sum_{j=1}^{n} \phi_j(u) \phi_j(v) e^{\lambda_j}` where :math:`\phi_j` are eigenvectors and :math:`\lambda_j` are eigenvalues of the adjacency matrix. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, return the communicability as a nested dictionary. Currently only dictionary return is supported. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict[int, dict[int, float]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Nested dictionary where `result[u][v]` is the communicability between nodes `u` and `v`. Values are always positive. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is directed or has self-loops. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} - only works on undirected graphs without self-loops - time complexity: `O(n³)` for eigendecomposition + `O(n²)` for result - space complexity: `O(n²)` for matrices and results - communicability is symmetric: `C(u, v) = C(v, u)` - self-communicability `C(u, u) > 0` (related to subgraph centrality) - higher values indicate more "paths" (walks of all lengths) between nodes ## Examples {.doc-examples} Adjacent nodes have more walks connecting them than nodes two hops apart, so their communicability score comes out higher: ::: {#891bbab8 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec # Create a path graph: 1 -- 2 -- 3 graph = ec.Graph(directed=False) graph.add_node(label="1") graph.add_node(label="2") graph.add_node(label="3") graph.add_edge("1", "2") graph.add_edge("2", "3") comm = graph.communicability() id1 = graph.get_id_from_label("1") id2 = graph.get_id_from_label("2") id3 = graph.get_id_from_label("3") comm[id1][id2], comm[id1][id3] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (1.3682988720085911, 0.5890917783042856) ``` ::: ::: Summing a node's communicability with every other node gives a sense of how well connected it is overall -- unsurprisingly high for a hub: ::: {#85c228f0 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph(directed=False) graph.add_node(label="A") graph.add_node(label="B") graph.add_node(label="C") graph.add_node(label="D") graph.add_edge("A", "B") graph.add_edge("B", "C") graph.add_edge("B", "D") comm = graph.communicability() b_id = graph.get_id_from_label("B") sum(comm[b_id].values()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 7.656337130875942 ``` ::: :::
